evidence: 007 (swarm-14, no diff): filter tools at discovery; re-resolve + re-check capability at call time (TOCTOU); fail closed on missing context; ambiguous not-found/not-authorized; policy delegates to PING capability authority. File: src/tenanos/tools/auth_boundary.ts.

093 (proposed, diffs/P-20260923-093.diff): typed side-effect classification registry + fail-closed guard + falsification tests. src/tenanos/tool-safety/. dispatch() consults a Lookup per dispatch; test 10 proves per-dispatch re-check of a revoked capability.

Overlap element (real but partial): 007 call-recheck vs 093 per-dispatch lookup. 093 dispatch(req, lookup) re-consults the lookup on every dispatch, so a grant-backed lookup already closes the cached-catalog TOCTOU that 007 names.

Distinct in 007, absent in 093: (a) discovery-time LIST filtering (FastMCP AuthMiddleware): unauthorized tools are invisible at catalog time. 093 gates only at dispatch; the worker still sees the full catalog. (b) Ambiguity rule: not-found and not-authorized produce the identical exterior denial (no existence leakage). 093 dispatch() returns distinct reason strings for unclassified vs UNKNOWN vs revoked, which leaks classification state. (c) Missing auth context as a first-class fail-closed input. (d) Explicit delegation of grant resolution to the live PING CapabilityAuthority; 093's lookup is the static classification registry, not live grant state.
Distinct in 093, absent in 007: effect-class enforcement, confirmation/idempotency requirements, envelope normalization (E3), retry discipline, timeout/OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, fail-closed audit.

File scope: src/tenanos/tools/auth_boundary.ts is unclaimed by any other proposal (verified against STATE.json); src/tenanos/tools/ does not exist on the integration branch; 093 lives in src/tenanos/tool-safety/. No file overlap.
No conflict: both agree policy/grant authority stays with the existing CapabilityAuthority and neither forks it.
notes: Implementation at impl/P-20260923-007/: auth_boundary.ts (strict TS) + jest test proving (1) discovery hides ungranted tools, (2) mid-run revocation is caught at call time, (3) unknown-tool vs unauthorized-tool denials are byte-identical, (4) missing context fails closed, (5) a throwing resolver fails closed. GrantResolver is injected; the module never grants and creates no authority.

overlaps.resolution: 007's call-recheck is the grant-backed GrantResolver that feeds 093's dispatch() as its per-dispatch Lookup. Single resolution path; no double-gating divergence.

scope_split.P-20260923-007: AUTH boundary: who may see/call. Discovery list-filtering, live grant resolution against the PING CapabilityAuthority, missing-context fail-closed, ambiguity-safe (opaque) exterior denials.
scope_split.P-20260923-093: SAFETY boundary: effect classes, confirmation/idempotency enforcement, envelope normalization, retry/timeout discipline, fail-closed audit.
scope_split.contract: Both the discovery filter and the dispatch lookup resolve against the SAME GrantResolver instance. A tool visible at discovery but denied at dispatch (or vice versa) is a wiring bug, not a policy disagreement.
scope_split.tension: 093's distinct dispatch denial reasons vs 007's ambiguity rule. Resolution: 007's opaque denial is the exterior-facing shape; 093's granular reasons stay internal to audit records. Recorded as failure class in scratch/failures-E3.md.
